children: Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - September 23, 2026) -
NRED Intelligent Mining Inc.

(OTCQB: NREDF) (the "Company" or "NRED") is pleased to provide a comprehensive technical and exploration update for its Wilmac Copper-Gold Project in the Similkameen Mining Division near Princeton, British Columbia.

The updated technical review builds upon the previous work completed on the Wilmac Project and incorporates additional geological, geophysical, geochemical and historical exploration information across the approximately 16,078-hectare (39,729-acre) property.
The updated work, prepared by Richard T. Walker, P.Geo.
provides an expanded and prioritized exploration framework identifying multiple copper-gold targets recommended for future drill testing.

The technical interpretation indicates that the Wilmac Project is prospective for one or more comparatively shallowly buried alkalic copper-gold porphyry centres within a multi-phase Late Triassic arc system. These interpretations remain exploration-stage hypotheses requiring drill testing and do not constitute evidence of an economic mineral deposit.

A two-phase exploration program totalling approximately $3.13 million has been proposed, including approximately $1.31 million for Phase I exploration and geophysical work and approximately $1.83 million for Phase II drilling
Wilmac - Priority Drill Target

Wilmac represents the Company's highest-priority exploration area. The technical interpretation identifies the trench-area system as the strongest direct relationship between sampled surface copper and an underlying geophysical system on the property.

The proposed exploration program includes drilling one or more of the strongest untrenched high-chargeability cores west and southwest of the existing trenches to test whether known surface copper mineralization strengthens into the underlying geophysical targets.
A separate approximately 350-400 metre inclined hole is proposed through the Wilmac quiet-resistive target, designed to also enter higher-chargeability material beneath or adjacent to it.
Lamont - Large Multi-Dataset Target
Ground IP and AMT surveying at Lamont has defined strong northwest-southeast oriented elongate chargeability pods that coalesce into a broader northeastern mass.

The target is supported by multiple datasets, including IP, AMT, soil geochemistry and three-dimensional geometry. The proposed program includes oriented, inclined drilling, including at least one deeper test to approximately 500 metres
Trojan-Condor - Deeper System to be Tested
The Trojan-Condor Corridor contains a large chargeability system along the northwestern margin of an interpreted magnetic complex.
Historical drilling intersected pyritic alteration and weak to locally anomalous copper mineralization, however, the holes were terminated at shallow depths relative to the preferred deeper model.

The updated exploration framework proposes testing the C1/C2 system with an inclined 450-550 metre hole through the chargeability core and intrusive-margin geometry, while also evaluating the potential to deepen the existing Eagle hole (WS14-004) by approximately 250 metres, where technically practical.
Established Copper-Gold District
The Wilmac Project is situated in the Quesnellia geological terrane of southern British Columbia, approximately 10 kilometres west of the Copper Mountain Mine
Geochemical relationships and overlapping approximately 204-205 Ma ages support interpretation of the property within the same broader Late Triassic magmatic-metallogenic province.

The Company cautions that this regional geological relationship does not demonstrate physical continuity, a common intrusive system or equivalent mineralization between Wilmac and Copper Mountain. Mineralization or resources at nearby properties are not necessarily indicative of mineralization at Wilmac.
Defined Path Toward Drilling
The technical work provides NRED with a staged exploration strategy combining the results of targeted geophysics, geochemistry and/or drilling.

The proposed initial drill holes are designed to serve as tests of the respective geological model interpreted for each separate and distinct grid in the context of the overall model interpreted for the Property. Evaluation of each drill hole will include systematic logging, multi-element analysis of recovered drill core (including copper-gold + pathfinder analysis) and magnetic susceptibility measurements, all of which are intended to further refine the three-dimensional interpretation of the property.
Management Commentary

Brian Goss, President and CEO of NRED Intelligent Mining, commented, "The technical work represents an important advancement for Wilmac and builds upon previous work completed on the project. By integrating additional geological, geochemical and geophysical information, we now have an increasingly refined exploration framework and a clearly prioritized portfolio of targets.

What is particularly encouraging is that our highest-priority Wilmac target combines known copper mineralization at surface with multiple supporting technical datasets. The scale and geometry of the systems identified at Lamont and Trojan-Condor provide additional opportunities for systematic testing across this large property.

With clearly defined exploration priorities and drill recommendations, NRED is positioned to advance Wilmac from target definition toward the critical next stage of testing these geological models through drilling."
Option Agreement Status

The Wilmac copper-gold project comprises 16,078 hectares located southwest of Princeton and approximately 10 kilometres west of Hudbay Minerals Inc.'s producing Copper Mountain Mine. NRED hold an interest in the Project pursuant to two option agreements concerning what are known as (1) the Wilmac and Lamont claims and (2) the Trojan-Condor Corridor claims.

The Company was required to make a $50,000 cash payment by December 1, 2025 and a second $125,000 cash payment by September 1, 2026 in order to keep the first option agreement in good standing, and was required to make a cash payment of $100,000 and to fund exploration expenditures of $100,000 on August 31, 2026 to keep the second option agreement in good standing. NRED has not made any of these payments and the option agreements are currently not in good standing. The optionors of the claims comprising the Project have not provided the Company with notice of termination, but may do so on seven day's notice.
Qualified Person

The scientific and technical information in this news release, including the geological interpretations described herein, has been reviewed and approved by Rick Walker, P.Geo., a Qualified Person as defined by National Instrument 43-101 ("NI 43-101"). Mr. Walker is not independent of the Company within the meaning of NI 43-101.

About NRED Intelligent Mining Inc.
NRED Intelligent Mining Inc.

(OTCQB: NREDF) is a mineral exploration company focused on the identification, acquisition, exploration and development of copper-gold porphyry projects in British Columbia, leveraging an artificial intelligence-enhanced geospatial technology platform that it developed to identify and evaluate prospective mineral properties. The Company's optioned Wilmac copper-gold project comprises 16,078 hectares located within the Quesnel porphyry belt in the Similkameen Mining Division, southwest of Princeton and approximately 10 kilometres west of Hudbay Minerals Inc.'s producing Copper Mountain Mine.

Readers are cautioned that the discussion of mineralization, alteration or grades on adjacent, similar or analogous properties, including the Copper Mountain Mine, is not necessarily indicative of the mineralization or potential of the Wilmac Copper-Gold Project. The Company has no interest in, or right to acquire any interest in, any such properties.
